newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy can meet EMU CPI, rate goals - ISTAT chief.
newsitem.headline: Italy can meet EMU CPI, rate goals - ISTAT chief.

text.p: The head of Italian statistics institute ISTAT said Italy was certain to come within the inflation and interest rate parameters required for joining a single European currency at its start.
But ISTAT head Alberto Zuliani said fulfilling other criteria, like ratios on state deficit and debt to gross domestic product (GDP), could be problematic.
Asked by reporters at a meeting which economic and monetary union criteria Italy would achieve, Zuliani replied: "As regards inflation and long term interest rates, certainly yes."
"The other parameters are much more problematic," he added.
Countries wishing to join a single European currency at its planned 1999 start are required to have low inflation and long term interest rates.
In addition they should have a debt to GDP ratio under 60 percent and a budget deficit ratio to GDP of three percent.
Italy has a debt to GDP ratio of around 120 percent while its budget deficit was about 7.5 percent of GDP last year.
